lessons.title: Station Notices: Maintenance and Service Updates
lessons.objective: Learners will understand the meanings of carry out maintenance and out of service in a station notice and use them in natural workplace messages.

reading.text: The station manager will carry out maintenance on the north entrance escalator next Tuesday. While the work is underway, the escalator will be out of service and signs will direct passengers to the lifts. Staff will inspect the warning boards before the morning rush and report any blocked route to the duty manager. The notice asks passengers to allow a few extra minutes when changing platforms.

sentences.text: The station manager will carry out maintenance on the north entrance escalator next Tuesday.
While the work is underway, the escalator will be out of service and signs will direct passengers to the lifts.
Staff will inspect the warning boards before the morning rush and report any blocked route to the duty manager.
The notice asks passengers to allow a few extra minutes when changing platforms.

targets.meaningEn: to perform work to repair or keep equipment in good condition
not working or not available for use

exercises.prompt: In sentence s1, 'The station manager will carry out maintenance on the north entrance escalator next Tuesday,' what does 'carry out maintenance' mean?

options.text: It means to check and repair the escalator to keep it in good condition.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches performing work to keep equipment in good condition.

options.text: It means to build a new north entrance for the station.
options.explanation: Wrong because building a new entrance means construction, not keeping equipment in good condition.

options.text: It means to close the whole station and stop all trains on Tuesday.
options.explanation: Wrong because closing the station means stopping service, not performing repair work.

exercises.explanation: The context is repair work on the escalator to keep it working.

exercises.prompt: Choose the natural sentence using 'carry out maintenance'.

options.text: The technicians will carries out maintenance on the air conditioners tomorrow.
options.explanation: Wrong because after 'will' the verb must be 'carry', not 'carries'.

options.text: The technicians will carry out a maintenance on the air conditioners tomorrow.
options.explanation: Wrong because 'maintenance' is uncountable here, so remove 'a'.

options.text: The technicians will carry out maintenance on the air conditioners tomorrow.
options.explanation: Correct because verb form, collocation, and word order are natural.

exercises.explanation: Only one option uses the phrase with correct grammar and collocation.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s2, 'While the work is underway, the escalator will be out of service,' what does 'out of service' mean?

options.text: It means the escalator will stay open for passengers but run more slowly during the morning rush.
options.explanation: Wrong: the notice directs passengers to the lifts while work is underway; it does not say they can keep using the escalator at a slower speed.

options.text: It means passengers will not be able to use the escalator while the work is underway.
options.explanation: Correct: the notice directs passengers to the lifts, so the escalator is unavailable to them during the work.

options.text: It means the escalator will be free for passengers to use during the maintenance work.
options.explanation: Wrong: the notice directs passengers to the lifts during the work, so it does not say the escalator remains available to passengers.

exercises.explanation: Here, out of service means passengers cannot use the escalator during the maintenance; the notice tells them to use the lifts.

exercises.prompt: Choose the natural sentence using 'out of service'.

options.text: The lift is out of services, so please take the stairs to the second floor.
options.explanation: Wrong because the fixed phrase needs singular 'service', not 'services'.

options.text: The lift is out of service, so please take the stairs to the second floor.
options.explanation: Correct because grammar, spelling, and the fixed phrase are natural.

options.text: The lift out of service, so please take the stairs to the second floor.
options.explanation: Wrong because the sentence is missing 'is' before 'out of service'.

exercises.explanation: Only one option uses the fixed phrase with correct grammar.

exercises.prompt: You are an office assistant. Write 2-3 sentences to a colleague explaining that the main office printer is unavailable and suggesting another printer to use.
exercises.sampleAnswer: Our main printer is out of service this morning. Please use the printer on the second floor until it is fixed.
selfCheck: I used the phrase 'out of service' to describe the printer.
exercises.explanation: Compare with the model and self-assess; no automatic grade.
